newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rebounds but remains bearish.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rebounds but remains bearish.

text.p: Singapore middle distillate prices rebounded marginally on bargain hunting Thursday as buyers found a short-term floor to prices, but traders said the overall sentiment remained bearish and values might dip further.
After Wednesday's deal at a low $21.45 per barrel for early July, a European major sold another cargo today at $21.60 per barrel for July 4-8 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis to a Chinese trader.

The Chinese trader has been an active buyer over the past two weeks. Early last week it bought a cargo from a South Korean trader at 65 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight Fuzhou basis.
The Chinese trader also bought a cargo from a Japanese trader last week at $177 per tonne, c-and-f southern China.
Traders said the European major also sold a cargo into southern China this week at $168 per tonne, c-and-f basis, which might have also been sold to the same trader.
They said the Chinese trader might have buying outlets from endusers in China.

They said c-and-f values into southern China is now testing the $160 per tonne mark as buying remained scattered, spooked by talk that China's national refiner SINOPEC have decided not to allow importers to use last year's outstanding import quota beyond July. China has so far allowed importers to use 1996 import quotas for the first and second quarters of this year.
The market was also rife with talk that SINOPEC might not issue new import quotas for the third and fourth quarters to encourage sales from domestic refineries.
Traders also said stocks in China and Hong Kong remained high with offers to Hong Kong seen at 20 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f basis, compared with 70 cents two weeks ago.
India has issued a tender to buy gas oil for August delivery, which closes on July 3.

Taipei sources said that state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp might defer issuing its tender to sell gas oil for July-December liftings until August because of current low prices. It might issue another tender to sell a third cargo for July instead. A decision would be known by Friday, the sources said.

Jet fuel was also offered higher by a European major at $23.70 and $23.90 for July lifting, facing a bid from a Singapore trader at $23.10 for second-half July lifting, compared with Wednesday's deal at $23.00.
Traders said the physical jet/gas oil regrade has widened over $1.50, indicating the stronger tone on jet as regional demand was seen as steady.
Traders said while Indonesia was expected to take up to two million barrels for July, about 450,000 barrels will be from its term contract with Kuwait.
Most of its July gas oil demand, estimated at four million barrels, were also expected to come from term contracts.
